papers.title: stFormer integrates spatial ligand signaling into a foundation model for spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Recent foundation models for single-cell transcriptomic data generate informative, context-aware gene and cell representations. Spatial transcriptomic (ST) data offer extra positional insights but were not considered by these single-cell models. We introduce stFormer, a transformer model tailored for ST data, which employs the cross-attention module to incorporate spatial ligand genes. To unify different ST technologies with a trade-off between resolution and gene coverage, we propose a biased cross-attention method that enables the model to do learning with single-cell resolution on whole-tra
papers.summary: stFormer is a transformer-based foundation model designed specifically for spatial transcriptomics data, using cross-attention to incorporate spatial ligand signaling genes. It introduces a biased cross-attention method to handle the trade-off between resolution and gene coverage across different ST technologies, enabling single-cell resolution learning on whole-transcriptome data. This allows the model to generate context-aware gene and cell representations that account for spatial signaling interactions.

papers.title: CDKPredict: a clinicogenomic model for risk-adapted therapeutic intervention in breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Wide variation in outcomes is observed for patients with hormone-receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer (MBC) receiving first-line CDK4/6 inhibitors plus endocrine therapy (CDK4/6i+ET). Although front-line escalation strategies are beginning to enter clinical practice, assigning patients to intensified or de-intensified approaches remains challenging due to several mechanisms of resistance spanning tumor-intrinsic and host factors. To address this, we developed CDKPredict, an interpretable machine-learning model integrating baseline clinicopathologic and genomic features to predict outcome
papers.summary: CDKPredict is an interpretable machine-learning model that integrates baseline clinicopathologic and genomic features to predict outcomes for patients with hormone-receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer receiving first-line CDK4/6 inhibitors plus endocrine therapy. The model aims to help clinicians assign patients to intensified or de-intensified treatment strategies, addressing the challenge of variable outcomes and multiple resistance mechanisms.

papers.title: Disease relevance and replicability of deep learning gene expression prediction.
papers.abstract: Recent deep learning (DL) models predict average gene expression levels from DNA sequences with high overall correlation to measured values. We examine these DL models through the lens of disease research. The seemingly high overall performance of DL models is largely due to capturing whether genes are "On" or "Off", and to a lesser extent, disease-relevant expression level changes for "On" genes. Indeed, the more bimodal the gene expression distribution, the better the reported performance. We track the extent of this issue across tissues, molecular systems, and cancers. Compounding the model
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint evaluates deep learning models that predict gene expression from DNA sequence, showing their high reported correlations largely reflect predicting whether genes are on or off rather than fine-grained expression levels. Performance is inflated for genes with bimodal expression and is weaker for disease-relevant expression changes, raising concerns about the models' utility and replicability in disease research.

papers.title: Biological rationales from language models enable leakage-resistant forecasts of target-indication success.
papers.abstract: Identifying which target-indication (T-I) hypotheses can translate into clinical success remains a central challenge in drug discovery. We present PRIORITI (Prospective Rationale-Informed Outcome Reasoning for Integrated Target-indication Intelligence), a leakage-resistant framework that separates upstream biological evidence synthesis from outcome prediction. Given only a target gene and disease indication, a domain-instructed large language model (LLM) synthesizes drug-agnostic human genetics across prespecified channels. These evidence were embedded and combined with static entity context d
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors introduce PRIORITI, a framework that uses a domain-instructed large language model to synthesize drug-agnostic human genetic evidence for a given target-indication pair, then predicts clinical success from these embeddings. By separating upstream biological evidence synthesis from outcome prediction, the approach aims to avoid data leakage and provide more realistic forecasts of which drug targets will succeed clinically.

papers.title: AI-Based Comparison of UniProt annotations and Literature Across Human Kinases.
papers.abstract: Curated protein records and their supporting publications organize biological evidence at different levels of detail. Here, we used AI to independently answer a set of biological questions using either UniProt records or the full texts of the literature cited by those records, and then used AI-based evaluation to compare the resulting answers in terms of information coverage and semantic agreement. Fifty human proteins were selected from ten groups in a kinase sequence collection. Target-identity filtering retained 1,749 protein-publication records representing 1,655 distinct publications. For
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint uses AI to compare the information content of UniProt protein records against the full texts of the publications they cite, focusing on 50 human kinases. The authors find differences in coverage and semantic agreement between curated database annotations and primary literature, highlighting where curated records may omit or diverge from published evidence. The work demonstrates an AI-driven approach for auditing biological knowledge resources.

papers.title: Transformer-based decision support with CNN and ViT for prognostic risk stratification following adjuvant chemotherapy in high-grade glioma: a multicenter study.
papers.abstract: High-grade gliomas (HGGs) exhibit marked intratumoral heterogeneity, which is associated with variable survival outcomes among patients receiving standard adjuvant chemotherapy. Conventional methods relying on molecular biomarkers are constrained by technical limitations and tumor heterogeneity. This study aimed to develop a multi-channel 2.5D deep learning framework that integrates Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Vision Transformer (ViT) features to noninvasively stratify HGG patients based on expected survival outcomes following postoperative adjuvant temozolomide (TMZ) chemotherapy a
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: This study develops a multi-channel 2.5D deep learning framework combining CNN and Vision Transformer features to noninvasively stratify high-grade glioma patients by expected survival after adjuvant temozolomide chemotherapy. The approach aims to overcome limitations of conventional molecular biomarker-based stratification, which is hampered by tumor heterogeneity and technical constraints, and is validated across multiple centers.

papers.title: AcrSeek: Metric Learning with Hybrid Negative Mining for Anti-CRISPR Protein Detection under Extreme Class Imbalance.
papers.abstract: Anti-CRISPR (Acr) proteins inhibit CRISPR-Cas immunity and are key targets for precise control of CRISPR-based genome editing and phage-host coevolution research. Their experimental identification is costly and low-throughput, so computational predictors are used to prioritise candidates for testing. In this setting validated positives number in the hundreds while phage-derived putative negatives reach tens of thousands, producing extreme class imbalance. Yet existing classification-based predictors train and evaluate on 1:1 balanced datasets and allow high-similarity sequences between trainin
papers.summary: AcrSeek is a computational tool for detecting anti-CRISPR (Acr) proteins, which inhibit CRISPR-Cas immunity and are useful for controlling genome editing. Unlike prior predictors that train on artificially balanced datasets, AcrSeek uses metric learning with hybrid negative mining to handle the extreme class imbalance (hundreds of positives vs. tens of thousands of negatives) and avoid overestimating performance from similar sequences. This makes it better suited for prioritizing candidate Acr proteins for experimental testing.

papers.title: CheckAMG: Accurate Identification of Auxiliary Viral Genes with Genome-Language Models.
papers.abstract: Viruses shape microbial metabolism through auxiliary viral genes (AVGs) that reprogram host metabolism, physiology, and gene regulation during infection. Identifying AVGs is complicated by ambiguous viral versus cellular assignment, inconsistent curation, and reliance on sequence homology that misses divergent functions. Here we present CheckAMG, which pairs annotation-based AVG prediction, curated with a per-gene viral scoring system and ontological mapping of metabolic function, with a finetuned genome-language model for annotation-independent discovery. Benchmarked against DRAM-V and VIBRAN
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: CheckAMG is a new tool that identifies auxiliary viral genes (AVGs) by combining annotation-based prediction with a fine-tuned genome-language model, addressing the ambiguity between viral and cellular gene assignment and the limitations of homology-based methods. It uses a per-gene viral scoring system and ontological mapping of metabolic functions, and is benchmarked against existing tools DRAM-V and VIBRANT. The approach enables more accurate discovery of divergent AVGs that reprogram host metabolism during infection.

papers.title: Agentic campaign control for high-throughput de novo binder design.
papers.abstract: Progress in artificial intelligence has produced a rapidly growing ecosystem of methods for de novo protein design. With access to many specialized and often complementary tools, how does one use them effectively, especially with a finite compute budget? Here, we introduce Target-adaptive Rescue-Explore-eXploit (T-REX) , an agentic protein binder design framework that orchestrates multiple state-of-the-art protein generative models and structure evaluators. Over the course of a design campaign, T-REX leverages large language model (LLM) agents to reason over accumulating outcomes and decide wh
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: T-REX is an agentic framework that uses LLM agents to orchestrate multiple protein generative models and structure evaluators for de novo binder design, adaptively deciding which tools to run as results accumulate. It aims to make high-throughput binder design campaigns more effective under finite compute budgets by balancing rescue, exploration, and exploitation strategies.

papers.title: CardioChrom Reconstructs the Human Cardiac Virtual Epigenome from Single-Nucleus Transcriptomes.
papers.abstract: Matched epigenomic profiling remains scarce in human heart failure, limiting regulatory interpretation of single-nucleus ribonucleic acid (RNA) sequencing data. We developed CardioChrom, a cardiac-specialized framework that reconstructs chromatin accessibility, histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation (H3K27ac), and histone H3 lysine 27 trimethylation (H3K27me3) from single-nucleus RNA profiles.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: CardioChrom is a cardiac-specialized computational framework that reconstructs three epigenomic modalities (chromatin accessibility, H3K27ac, and H3K27me3) directly from single-nucleus RNA sequencing profiles of human heart tissue. This enables regulatory interpretation of snRNA-seq data in heart failure, where matched epigenomic profiling is scarce.

papers.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Protein Language Models Reveals Encoded Structural and Functional Properties of Intrinsically Disordered Proteins.
papers.abstract: Protein language models (PLMs) such as ESM-2 encode protein sequences as embeddings for downstream tasks. PLMs are trained on a masked learning objective that leverages evolutionary constraints. While interpretability studies of ESM-2 have focused on folded proteins, their behavior on intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs), which constitute a substantial fraction of the human proteome and are implicated in numerous diseases, remains understudied. Because IDPs experience different types of evolutionary constraints on their amino acid sequences, we hypothesized that PLMs would behave different
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint investigates how the protein language model ESM-2 internally represents intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs), which lack fixed 3D structure but make up a large portion of the human proteome and are linked to many diseases. Using mechanistic interpretability techniques, the authors show that ESM-2's embeddings encode structural and functional properties specific to IDPs, despite the model being trained primarily on evolutionary constraints from folded proteins. This suggests PLMs capture biologically meaningful information about disordered regions that could aid disease-related research.

papers.title: GeoEPred: A multimodal structure-aware geometric deep learning framework for Gram-negative bacterial secreted effector prediction with sequence semantics.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of effector proteins secreted by Gram-negative bacteria is important for elucidating bacterial pathogenic mechanisms and developing precise anti-infective strategies. Although existing methods have benefited from the strong sequence feature extraction capacity of pretrained protein language models, reliance on linear sequence information alone often fails to fully capture the three-dimensional conformational signals required for virulence functions. Meanwhile, conventional structure-based methods are limited by the scarcity of experimentally resolved protein structures. To
papers.summary: GeoEPred is a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts secreted effector proteins in Gram-negative bacteria by combining protein language model sequence embeddings with geometric features derived from predicted 3D structures. This structure-aware approach aims to overcome the limitations of sequence-only methods and the scarcity of experimental structures, improving effector identification for understanding bacterial pathogenesis.

papers.title: Dynamic Fourier wavelet positional encoding for anticancer peptide prediction via transfer learning.
papers.abstract: Computational identification of anti-tumor peptides (ACPs) is challenged by limited training data and the multi-scale nature of biological sequences. Standard transformer positional encodings fail to capture the periodicities and local motifs that govern peptide function. We propose dynamic Fourier wavelet positional encoding (DFWPE), which replaces fixed sinusoidal encodings with parallel adaptive Fourier and multi-scale wavelet branches, fused by a context-aware gating mechanism. A dual-stage transfer learning strategy pre-trains on 5,785 curated peptide sequences before fine-tuning on ACP74
papers.summary: The authors introduce dynamic Fourier wavelet positional encoding (DFWPE), a transformer positional encoding scheme that combines adaptive Fourier and multi-scale wavelet branches via context-aware gating to better capture periodicities and local motifs in peptide sequences. Using a dual-stage transfer learning strategy, they pre-train on 5,785 curated peptides and fine-tune for anticancer peptide prediction, aiming to overcome limited training data and the multi-scale nature of biological sequences.

papers.title: Multiscale cross modal fusion and cascaded signal propagation for drug target interaction prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target interaction (DTI) facilitates the translation of lead compounds into clinical therapeutics. Despite progress in deep learning, two challenges remain: the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein modalities and insufficient use of complementary knowledge from pretrained encoders. To address these issues, we propose SF-DTI, a unified framework that integrates multi-encoder protein fusion, structure-semantic drug alignment, and progressive cross-modal refinement for DTI prediction. Specifically, SF-DTI captures global protein semantics from mult
papers.summary: The authors present SF-DTI, a deep learning framework for predicting drug-target interactions that combines multiple protein encoders, aligns drug structure with semantic representations, and progressively refines cross-modal features. The approach aims to bridge the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein modalities and better exploit complementary knowledge from pretrained encoders.

papers.title: Revealing the toxicological effects and mechanisms of tris(1-chloro-2-propyl) phosphate exposure on osteoarthritis based on network toxicology, machine learning, and molecular docking.
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative disease affecting all joints in the body, impacting over 500 million people globally and imposing a significant healthcare burden. Tris(1-chloro-2-propyl) phosphate (TCPP), one of the widely used organophosphate flame retardants (OPFRs), exhibits notable environmental and biological toxicity. However, the role and molecular mechanisms of TCPP exposure in OA remain unclear. This study combined network toxicology, machine learning, and molecular docking techniques to identify key targets and pathways associated with TCPP exposure and OA. A nomogram model was
papers.summary: This study integrates network toxicology, machine learning, and molecular docking to identify key targets and pathways linking exposure to the flame retardant TCPP with osteoarthritis. The authors construct a nomogram model to predict TCPP-related OA risk and highlight candidate molecular mechanisms. The work suggests environmental pollutant exposure may contribute to OA pathogenesis through specific target genes and pathways.

papers.title: Machine learning-assisted directed evolution of plant Rubisco.
papers.abstract: Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (Rubisco) is foundational to life on Earth, catalyzing carbon dioxide (CO2) fixation to generate biomass. However, Rubisco is a slow and inefficient enzyme that has proven challenging to engineer. We applied the structure-informed machine learning (ML) model ESM-IF1 to identify plausible amino acid sites in the large subunit of Nicotiana tabacum Rubisco to target for directed evolution. ML-assisted library design followed by selection in Rubisco-dependent Escherichia coli identified multiple enriched variants displaying improved catalytic efficie
papers.summary: This study uses the structure-informed machine learning model ESM-IF1 to guide directed evolution of the large subunit of tobacco Rubisco, identifying amino acid sites likely to improve enzyme function. Selection in Rubisco-dependent E. coli yielded multiple variants with improved catalytic efficiency. The work demonstrates that ML-assisted library design can overcome the difficulty of engineering this notoriously slow and inefficient carbon-fixing enzyme.

papers.title: Massively Multiplexed Photonic Chip With Cross-Channel Fusion For Harmonized Biosensing.
papers.abstract: Accurate, label-free analysis of complex biological mixtures is limited by poor multiplexing scalability and inconsistent responses across sensor samples. We introduce a transformative sensing platform that integrates large-scale photonic multiplexing with data-driven analytics to overcome these constraints. Our modular, affordable glass-chip whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) photonic architecture is designed to support simultaneous readout of up to 100 sensing channels comprising over 10 000 high-Q microresonators, exceeding existing multiplexing capabilities by more than two orders of magnitude.
papers.summary: The authors present a glass-chip photonic sensing platform based on whispering-gallery-mode microresonators that can read out up to 100 sensing channels containing over 10,000 high-Q resonators simultaneously, a multiplexing scale roughly two orders of magnitude beyond existing systems. They pair this hardware with data-driven cross-channel fusion analytics to harmonize responses across sensor samples, enabling accurate label-free analysis of complex biological mixtures.

papers.title: Pretrained spectrum representations for diverse tandem mass spectrometry proteomics tasks.
papers.abstract: Mass spectrometry is the dominant technology in the field of proteomics, enabling high-throughput analysis of the protein content of complex biological samples. Due to the complexity of the instrumentation and resulting data, sophisticated computational methods are required for the processing and interpretation of acquired mass spectra. Machine learning has shown great promise to improve the analysis of mass spectrometry data, with numerous purpose-built methods for improving specific steps in the data acquisition and analysis pipeline reaching widespread adoption. Each of these tasks rely on
papers.summary: This paper introduces pretrained spectrum representations that can be applied across diverse tandem mass spectrometry proteomics tasks, rather than building separate models for each step. The approach leverages transfer learning to improve performance on multiple downstream analyses of mass spectra. It represents a step toward general-purpose machine learning models in proteomics.

papers.title: VAEBAC: A representation-learning framework for proteome-scale prediction of amyloidogenic proteins and functional stratification of nucleic-acid-binding proteins.
papers.abstract: Nucleic-acid-binding proteins (NABPs) govern transcription, replication and genome organization, yet the distribution of aggregation susceptibility within regulatory proteomes remains unresolved. Here, we systematically examine amyloidogenic potential across the nucleic-acid-binding proteomes of four phylogenetically diverse organisms-Escherichia coli, Bacillus subtilis, Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Homo sapiens-spanning prokaryotes and eukaryotes, to determine whether aggregation-prone sequence architectures are selectively constrained within transcriptional networks.
papers.summary: VAEBAC is a representation-learning framework that predicts amyloidogenic potential across entire proteomes and applies it to nucleic-acid-binding proteins (NABPs) from four diverse organisms (E. coli, B. subtilis, S. cerevisiae, H. sapiens). The study systematically maps aggregation-prone sequence architectures within regulatory proteomes, revealing how amyloidogenic risk is distributed and potentially constrained across transcriptional networks in prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

papers.title: HINN prioritizes multi-omics biomarkers associated with cognitive decline.
papers.abstract: Integrating multi-omics data for disease prediction remains challenging due to the complexity of cross-layer biological interactions and the limited use of prior biological knowledge in many machine learning models. We present the Hierarchical Input Neural Network (HINN), a deep learning framework that incorporates biologically informed connections across genomic, epigenetic, and transcriptomic layers to model regulatory relationships in a structured and interpretable manner. HINN was applied to blood-derived multi-omics data to predict cognitive assessment scores, including MMSE, MoCA, ADAS11
papers.summary: The authors present HINN, a deep learning framework that encodes known biological regulatory relationships between genomic, epigenetic, and transcriptomic layers as structured connections in a neural network. Applied to blood-derived multi-omics data, HINN predicts cognitive assessment scores (MMSE, MoCA, ADAS11) and prioritizes biomarkers associated with cognitive decline. The approach aims to improve interpretability and leverage prior biological knowledge compared to standard machine learning models.

papers.title: Metabolic modeling: the link between AI and multi-omics data to accelerate the discovery of antibiotic-resistant traits in ESKAPE pathogens.
papers.abstract: The development of predictive understanding of bacterial resistance to antibiotics is one of the greatest challenges of modern medicine. Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) are mathematical representations of the metabolic network of a given organism assembled from genomic data that predict cellular activity across many environmental and genetic contexts. Because a single model can be solved under thousands of conditions, GEMs generate data at scales that support downstream analysis with artificial intelligence tools, helping to elucidate how pathogens adapt to host environments, evade immune
papers.summary: This review discusses how genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) of ESKAPE pathogens can be combined with AI and multi-omics data to predict antibiotic resistance traits. Because GEMs can simulate cellular behavior across thousands of conditions, they provide large-scale training data for machine learning approaches that link genotype, metabolism, and resistance phenotypes. The authors argue this integrated framework could accelerate discovery of resistance mechanisms and new therapeutic targets.

papers.title: DeepSAP: An Integrated Generative and Predictive Deep-Learning Framework for Controllable Design of Self-Assembling Peptides.
papers.abstract: Self-assembling peptides (SAPs), particularly short sequences whose amino acid composition dictates their spontaneous organisation, are emerging as versatile building blocks in biomedicine and bio-optoelectronic materials. As the thermodynamic and kinetic behaviours of peptide self-assembly are affected by intrinsic factors, such as amino acid sequence, length, and hydrophobicity, the controllable design of SAPs with tailored properties is essential to achieve specific structures and functions for various application scenarios. However, existing computational approaches, which primarily focus
papers.summary: DeepSAP is a deep-learning framework that combines generative and predictive models to design self-assembling peptides with controllable properties. It addresses the challenge of designing short peptides whose sequence dictates their spontaneous assembly into desired structures, a task limited by existing computational approaches.

papers.title: A self-supervised foundation model for large-scale zebrafish image analysis.
papers.abstract: High-throughput zebrafish screening generates large volumes of imaging data, creating a need for scalable computational methods that reduce dependence on manual annotation and repeated task-specific model development. In this study, we develop a self-supervised foundation model for zebrafish image analysis pretrained on more than 468,000 images from seven heterogeneous zebrafish imaging datasets spanning different developmental stages, imaging platforms, modalities, and experimental conditions. By learning a shared representation from diverse unlabeled zebrafish images, the proposed framework
papers.summary: This paper presents a self-supervised foundation model for zebrafish image analysis, pretrained on over 468,000 images from seven heterogeneous datasets covering different developmental stages, imaging platforms, and modalities. The model learns a shared representation from unlabeled images, reducing the need for manual annotation and task-specific model development in high-throughput zebrafish screening.

papers.title: Examining Protein Residue-Level Stability Using Theory and Experiment.
papers.abstract: Protein behavior, whether evolved in nature or intentionally designed, is governed by the energetics of amino acid interactions that bridge sequence to function. As an extension of the theory of protein folding funnels, local frustration quantifies the optimality of these residue-level interactions relative to alternatives. Although this framework has existed for decades, experimental validation has remained elusive. Past deep mutational scanning datasets enable experimental assessment across nearly 8,000 positions from 178 proteins. Results provide experimental evidence for theoretical predic
papers.summary: This study provides experimental validation of the local frustration framework, which quantifies how optimal residue-level interactions are in protein structures. Using deep mutational scanning data covering nearly 8,000 positions across 178 proteins, the authors show that theoretically predicted frustration correlates with experimental mutational effects. This bridges a long-standing gap between protein folding theory and empirical measurements.

papers.title: Explainable AI-driven marker selection and development of EastFocus AISNPplex 61 assay for fine-scale biogeographical ancestry inference.
papers.abstract: A hierarchical ancestry inference framework was developed to resolve continental and fine-scale East Asian population structures for forensic applications. Combining the shapley additive explanations (SHAP) method with recursive feature elimination, 58 ancestry informative single-nucleotide polymorphisms (AIM-SNPs) were selected. A self-developed 6-dye allele-specific PCR multiplex system (EastFocus AISNPplex 61) was established, integrating these AIM-SNPs, two Y-chromosomal InDels, and the Amelogenin locus. Validation demonstrated reliable single-source genotyping down to 250-500 pg and full
papers.summary: The authors developed a hierarchical ancestry inference framework that uses explainable AI (SHAP combined with recursive feature elimination) to select 58 ancestry-informative SNPs for resolving fine-scale East Asian population structure. They built a 6-dye allele-specific PCR multiplex assay (EastFocus AISNPplex 61) incorporating these SNPs plus Y-InDels and Amelogenin, validated for forensic use down to 250-500 pg of DNA. This provides a practical forensic tool for biogeographical ancestry inference at fine scales within East Asia.

papers.title: Time Series Segmentation in Adaptive Optics Ophthalmoscopy With Application to Flicker-Induced Vasodilation.
papers.abstract: To develop an automated image processing pipeline to segment retinal arterial walls in a series of adaptive optics ophthalmoscopy (AOO) images, overcoming difficulties related to various quality levels within the series, to accurately evaluate morphometric differences.
papers.summary: This paper presents an automated image processing pipeline that segments retinal arterial walls across time-series adaptive optics ophthalmoscopy (AOO) images, handling variable image quality to measure flicker-induced vasodilation. The method enables accurate morphometric comparison of vessel changes over time, supporting clinical studies of retinal vascular function.

papers.title: Snail shell-derived hydroxyapatite on ant clay: a sustainable solution for phosphate sequestration and circular agricultural reuse.
papers.abstract: In this study, a sustainable adsorbent comprising hydroxyapatite derived from snail shells and clay collected from ant nests was developed and used for the efficient removal of phosphate (PO4 3-) from aqueous solutions. The synthesized adsorbent was characterized using different characterization techniques like FTIR spectroscopy, XRD, SEM, TGA, PZC, and BET analysis to confirm its successful synthesis, morphology, thermal stability, surface charges, and surface area, respectively. The adsorbent was systematically investigated for phosphate adsorption by optimizing key experimental parameters,
papers.summary: This study develops a sustainable phosphate adsorbent by combining hydroxyapatite extracted from snail shells with clay from ant nests. The material was characterized using standard techniques and optimized for removing phosphate from water, supporting both pollution remediation and circular agricultural reuse of waste materials.

papers.title: ParaEM: Antigen-aware sequence-based paratope prediction with Expectation-Maximization.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of antibody paratopes-the residues contacting the antigen-is vital for understanding antibody-antigen recognition, antibody engineering, and vaccine design. However, structure-based predictors require antibody structural inputs, which are often obtained from experimentally determined antibody-antigen complexes in benchmark settings but are generally unavailable for new sequences. Conversely, sequence-based predictors scale efficiently but remain largely antigen-agnostic, limiting their use of pair-specific antigen context.
papers.summary: ParaEM is a new sequence-based method for predicting antibody paratopes (the residues that contact antigen) that incorporates antigen context, unlike prior sequence-based predictors that are largely antigen-agnostic. It uses an Expectation-Maximization framework to make antigen-aware predictions directly from antibody and antigen sequences, avoiding the need for structural inputs required by structure-based methods.

papers.title: ProFormer: generalizable classification of single-cell and plasma proteomes using deep learning.
papers.abstract: Proteins are the main drivers of cell function and disease, making proteomics a powerful technique for biomarker discovery and defining cell identity. While current technologies can profile thousands of proteins and reach single-cell sensitivity, limited throughput restricts applications such as robust classification of large biological or clinical cohorts. To close this gap, we present a deep-learning (DL) approach for the direct analysis of mass spectrometric (MS) data, assigning proteomic profiles to sample identity. Specifically, we introduce the ProFormer, a transformer pipeline that clas
papers.summary: ProFormer is a transformer-based deep learning pipeline that directly classifies proteomic profiles from mass spectrometry data, enabling sample identity assignment for both single-cell and plasma proteomes. This approach addresses throughput limitations in proteomics by allowing robust classification of large biological or clinical cohorts without extensive preprocessing.

papers.title: pLM-HP: Peptide hormone prediction using pre-trained protein language model representations.
papers.abstract: Peptide hormones play key roles in metabolic regulation, growth and development, and the maintenance of homeostasis and are important targets for drug discovery and design. However, traditional experimental methods for screening and identifying peptide hormones are costly and inefficient. Although existing machine learning methods have made some progress, they pay limited attention to class imbalance, and there is still room to improve prediction performance.
papers.summary: The paper introduces pLM-HP, a machine learning method that uses representations from a pre-trained protein language model to predict peptide hormones. It specifically addresses class imbalance, a problem under-addressed by prior methods, and reports improved prediction performance over existing approaches. The tool aims to speed up identification of peptide hormones, which are important drug-discovery targets.

papers.title: A Dynamics-Informed Machine Learning Framework for Inhibitor Optimization Against Quickly Evolving Targets to Avoid Resistance.
papers.abstract: Drug resistance often emerges through mutations that reshape protein conformational ensembles, allowing inhibitor potency to be altered without directly disrupting protein-ligand contacts. Consequently, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain difficult to identify, hindering the design of inhibitors with durable potency against rapidly evolving drug targets. To address this challenge, we developed ROBUST, a physics-informed machine learning framework that integrates experimental measurements, molecular dynamics simulations, and interpretable statistical modeling to identify en
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present ROBUST, a physics-informed machine learning framework that combines experimental binding data, molecular dynamics simulations, and interpretable statistical modeling to identify how mutations reshape protein conformational ensembles and alter inhibitor potency. The approach aims to guide the design of inhibitors that retain potency against rapidly evolving drug targets and avoid resistance.

papers.title: Screening for patients at risk for cardiac amyloidosis via electronic health records: A multicenter machine learning development and validation study.
papers.abstract: Timely detection is crucial to improve outcomes in patients with cardiac amyloidosis (CA) by initiation of guideline-directed disease-modifying treatments. Although confirmatory bone scintigraphy is highly accurate for CA detection, identifying at-risk patients for referral remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning model, Amylo-Detect, using structured multimodal electronic health record (EHR) data to guide referrals for confirmatory scintigraphy and monoclonal protein testing. Consecutive all-comer patients (n = 11,616) referred for bone scintigraphy at
papers.summary: This study developed and validated a machine learning model, Amylo-Detect, that uses structured multimodal electronic health record data to identify patients at risk for cardiac amyloidosis who should be referred for confirmatory bone scintigraphy and monoclonal protein testing. The model was developed and validated across multiple centers, aiming to improve timely detection and enable initiation of disease-modifying treatments.

papers.title: A serum proteomics-based predictive model for steroid-resistant immune checkpoint inhibitor associated myocarditis.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICIAM) is one of the immune-related adverse events (irAEs) with low incidence but extremely high mortality. High-dose glucocorticoid pulse therapy remains the recommended initial treatment for patients with ICIAM. However, an inadequate response to corticosteroid therapy is observed in some patients, who are subsequently classified as having steroid-resistant immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (srICIAM). Early combination of second-line immunosuppression may represent an effective therapeutic strategy. However, Biomarkers capa
papers.summary: This study uses serum proteomics to build a predictive model for identifying cancer patients who will not respond to steroid treatment for immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (srICIAM). Early identification of these steroid-resistant patients could enable timely addition of second-line immunosuppressive therapy, potentially reducing the high mortality associated with this rare but dangerous complication.

papers.title: Discovery of PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products through machine learning and structure-based screening.
papers.abstract: PIM-1 kinase, a serine/threonine kinase implicated in several cancers, has emerged as a promising yet underexplored target for anticancer therapy. This study aimed to identify the potential of PIM-1 inhibitors from marine natural products by integrating machine learning (ML)-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling with structure-based virtual screening.
papers.summary: This study combines machine learning-based QSAR modeling with structure-based virtual screening to identify PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products. PIM-1 is a promising anticancer target, and the integrated computational approach was used to prioritize marine compounds as potential inhibitors. The work demonstrates a hybrid screening strategy for natural product drug discovery.

papers.title: Omics data discovery agents: Agent-supported retrieval, reanalysis, and synthesis of published omics data.
papers.abstract: The biomedical literature contains a vast collection of omics studies, yet most published data remain functionally inaccessible for computational reuse. When raw data are deposited in public repositories, essential information for reproducing reported results is dispersed across main text, supplementary files, and code repositories, and in the rarer cases where intermediate data (e.g., protein abundance files) are shared, their location is irregular. Here we present an agentic framework for the agent-supported retrieval, reanalysis, and synthesis of published omics data. The system employs lar
papers.summary: The authors present an agentic framework that automates the retrieval, reanalysis, and synthesis of published omics data, addressing the problem that most published omics datasets remain inaccessible for computational reuse because key information is scattered across main text, supplements, and code repositories. The system uses LLM-based agents to locate and integrate these dispersed resources, enabling reproducible reanalysis at scale.

papers.title: Multi-Objective-Conditioned-Return-Blocks Decision Transformer: A Novel Approach for Multi-Objective De Novo Drug Design.
papers.abstract: Designing novel molecules that simultaneously satisfy several, often conflicting, properties is a long-standing challenge in drug design. While recent deep learning advances optimize single targets effectively, navigating the trade-offs required for multiple objectives remains a difficult problem.
papers.summary: The authors propose a novel decision transformer architecture, Multi-Objective-Conditioned-Return-Blocks, for de novo drug design that can simultaneously optimize multiple, often conflicting molecular properties. By conditioning on return blocks, the model navigates trade-offs between objectives, addressing a key limitation of existing single-target deep learning approaches.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of mitochondrial proteomes across the tree of life.
papers.abstract: Mitochondria arose from the endosymbiosis of a bacterium with an archaea-related host cell about 2 billion years ago. To understand their origins and evolution, we compared experimentally defined mitoproteomes from the MitoCarta Tree of Life project. Across eight organisms, we identified 8,619 distinct mitochondrial proteins within 3,199 families, of which 43% lack Pfam domains. We report 33 protein families conserved in eukaryotic pathogens yet absent in humans, representing promising candidate targets for protozoan infectious diseases. Leveraging our experimentally defined mitoproteomes, we
papers.summary: This study compares experimentally defined mitochondrial proteomes across eight organisms spanning the tree of life, identifying 8,619 distinct mitochondrial proteins in 3,199 families, with 43% lacking known Pfam domains. The authors highlight 33 protein families conserved in eukaryotic pathogens but absent in humans, offering potential new drug targets for protozoan diseases.

papers.title: Autoimmune disorders and cardiovascular disease: a matched cross-sectional analysis of disease-specific associations in Qatari primary care.
papers.abstract: Autoimmune disorders have been linked to increased cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk, but it is unclear whether the association is uniform across conditions or is concentrated in specific diseases, and whether inflammatory markers add value in a Middle Eastern primary-care setting. We examined disease-specific associations between autoimmune disorders and recorded CVD, rather than building a prognostic prediction tool.
papers.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study examined whether the link between autoimmune disorders and cardiovascular disease varies by specific autoimmune condition in a Qatari primary-care population. Using matched analysis, the authors aimed to identify which autoimmune diseases are most strongly associated with CVD and whether inflammatory markers add predictive value in this Middle Eastern setting.

papers.title: ELE: Estimating tissue-specific long noncoding RNA gene essentiality using graph neural networks.
papers.abstract: A gene is essential if its loss of function results in lethality, reduced fitness, or disease. Essential genes have attracted increasing attention due to their vital functions in biological systems. Many efforts have been made to find essential protein-coding genes. In complex organisms, the majority of the genome does not encode proteins. Noncoding genes play vital roles in many biological processes. Investigating the essentiality of noncoding genes is necessary. We present ELE (estimating long noncoding RNA essentiality), the first computational model for finding essential long noncoding RNA
papers.summary: ELE is the first computational model designed to predict the essentiality of long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) genes, which have been largely overlooked compared to protein-coding genes. It uses graph neural networks to estimate tissue-specific lncRNA essentiality, filling a gap in understanding the functional importance of noncoding genomic elements.

papers.title: Combating antimicrobial resistance through multimodal data via artificial intelligence.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a critical global health challenge, leading to substantial mortality and economic losses without science-based interventions. Conventional approaches to combating AMR have important limitations in addressing this escalating threat. Recent advances in AI, including deep learning, large language models, and protein language models, provide new opportunities to integrate multimodal data for AMR research. However, evidence remains uneven, with many approaches limited to computational benchmarking rather than real-world validation. Here, we critically review AI
papers.summary: This review critically examines how artificial intelligence—including deep learning, large language models, and protein language models—can integrate multimodal data to combat antimicrobial resistance. It highlights that while these approaches offer new opportunities, much of the evidence remains limited to computational benchmarking rather than real-world validation.

papers.title: Photonic AI for deeper understanding of the Planck epoch.
papers.abstract: This article addresses the requirements for a photonic artificial intelligence (AI) capable of supporting a deeper understanding of the Planck epoch in the origin of the Universe. The article continues the previous author's articles, which outlined requirements for AI to support studies of protein evolution on Earth, cosmic strings (CS) detection, and a non-standard view on the photon's nature. Modern digital generative AI cannot support its solution due to a lack of training datasets and limited energy resources for conducting adequate physical experiments. This article analyses the states of
papers.summary: This article argues that current digital generative AI is inadequate for studying the Planck epoch of the universe due to missing training data and energy constraints, and proposes that photonic AI could enable deeper physical understanding of this earliest cosmic era. It is a conceptual/position piece continuing the author's prior work on AI for protein evolution and cosmic string detection, rather than a report of new experimental or computational results.

papers.title: A palmitoylation-associated three-gene signature predicts prognosis, immune features, and drug sensitivity in gastric cancer: functional validation of CTHRC1.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is a heterogeneous malignancy that requires improved molecular tools for prognostic stratification. Protein palmitoylation regulates membrane localization and signaling, but the clinical relevance of palmitoylation-related genes (PRGs) in GC remains unclear.
papers.summary: The authors built a three-gene prognostic signature based on palmitoylation-related genes to stratify gastric cancer patients by survival, immune features, and drug sensitivity, and experimentally validated CTHRC1 as a functionally relevant gene. This links protein palmitoylation biology to clinically useful risk prediction in gastric cancer.

papers.title: Benchmarking ensemble and deep learning models for drought-responsive gene prioritisation in rice using multi-omics data.
papers.abstract: Identifying drought-responsive genes is critical for climate-resilient crop breeding, yet computational gene-trait association often relies on single-omics or generalized genomic datasets. Optimal algorithm selection for high-dimensional, small multi-omics datasets also remains a persistent challenge. We present a machine learning framework that extends the QTG-Finder feature set by integrating transcriptomic and proteomic features to classify drought-responsive genes in rice. Using MBKBase annotations, we evaluated the ability of these models to prioritise 336 drought-responsive genes among 2
papers.summary: This study benchmarks ensemble and deep learning models for prioritizing drought-responsive genes in rice by integrating transcriptomic and proteomic features into an extended QTG-Finder framework. Using MBKBase annotations, the authors evaluate model performance on a small, high-dimensional multi-omics dataset of 336 drought-responsive genes. The work highlights the challenges of algorithm selection for such datasets and provides guidance for computational gene prioritization in crop breeding.

papers.title: Lightweight 2D-Convolutional Neural Network for Drug-Kinase Binding Affinity Prediction with Minimal Encoded Representations.
papers.abstract: Drug-kinase binding affinity (DKBA) prediction plays a crucial role in prioritizing compounds and reducing the time and financial resources required for drug discovery. However, many existing deep learning models rely on complex molecular representations, such as molecular graphs or pretrained embeddings, which may increase computational complexity and limit scalability.
papers.journal: Iranian journal of pharmaceutical research : IJPR
papers.summary: The authors propose a lightweight 2D convolutional neural network that predicts drug-kinase binding affinity using minimal encoded molecular representations, avoiding complex graph structures or pretrained embeddings. This approach aims to reduce computational cost and improve scalability for virtual screening in drug discovery.

papers.title: Integrated network toxicology and multi-omics profiling reveal cell cycle, DNA damage repair, and metabolic alterations in cyclophosphamide-induced premature ovarian insufficiency.
papers.abstract: Cyclophosphamide (CTX)-induced chemotherapy injury is a leading iatrogenic cause of premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) and a major barrier to fertility preservation. Yet the systems-level mechanisms underlying its reproductive toxicity remain poorly defined.
papers.summary: This study combines network toxicology with multi-omics profiling to investigate how cyclophosphamide causes premature ovarian insufficiency. The authors identify disruptions in cell cycle regulation, DNA damage repair, and metabolic pathways as key mechanisms underlying the reproductive toxicity. These findings provide a systems-level view of chemotherapy-induced ovarian damage that could inform fertility preservation strategies.

papers.title: ZBP1 contributes to IFN-β-induced PANoptosis-related skeletal muscle cell injury in dermatomyositis.
papers.abstract: Dermatomyositis (DM) is a systemic autoimmune disease characterized by cutaneous manifestations and inflammatory skeletal muscle injury. Dysregulated type I interferon signaling and regulated cell death pathways may converge to promote myofiber damage. PANoptosis integrates core components of pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis, but its contribution to DM remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether ZBP1 drives PANoptosis (a combined form of pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis) in skeletal muscle cells during dermatomyositis, a systemic autoimmune disease with inflammatory muscle injury. The authors link dysregulated type I interferon signaling to ZBP1-mediated cell death, suggesting a mechanism by which IFN-β contributes to myofiber damage.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning models for predicting New-onset acute organ injury within 48 hours of admission in patients with community-acquired acute cholangitis.
papers.abstract: Community-acquired acute cholangitis (CAAC) can progress to acute organ injury (AOI), increasing poor prognosis risk. This study aimed to develop machine learning models using clinical information obtained before AOI onset to predict new-onset AOI within 48 h after admission in patients with CAAC.
papers.summary: This study develops machine learning models that use routinely collected clinical data available at admission to predict which patients with community-acquired acute cholangitis will develop new acute organ injury within 48 hours. The models aim to support early risk stratification and timely intervention in this patient population.

papers.title: Benchmarking hyperparameter optimization strategies for crop genomic prediction.
papers.abstract: Genomic prediction has become an important approach for accelerating crop breeding by using genome-wide marker information to predict complex traits. However, the performance of genomic prediction models is influenced not only by model selection but also by hyperparameter optimization strategies, which have received limited attention in crop genomic prediction studies. Based on four crop datasets, including maize, rice, wheat, and foxtail millet, we evaluated the prediction performance and computational efficiency of six representative genomic prediction models under four hyperparameter optimi
papers.summary: This study benchmarks six genomic prediction models across four crop datasets (maize, rice, wheat, foxtail millet) using four hyperparameter optimization strategies. It finds that the choice of hyperparameter optimization method meaningfully affects both prediction accuracy and computational efficiency, an aspect often overlooked in crop breeding applications. The results provide practical guidance for selecting optimization strategies in genomic prediction pipelines.

papers.title: Multi-omics graph attention network reveals neuro-immune-tumor pathways in breast cancer liver depression syndrome.
papers.abstract: Liver depression syndrome (LDS) is a core Chinese medicine (CM) syndrome implicated in the onset and progression of breast cancer, whose molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood, hindering further investigation.
papers.summary: This study applies a multi-omics graph attention network to investigate the molecular mechanisms linking liver depression syndrome (LDS), a core Chinese medicine syndrome, to breast cancer progression. The approach integrates multiple omics layers to uncover neuro-immune-tumor pathways associated with LDS. The findings aim to provide a systems-level understanding of how this syndrome influences breast cancer biology.

papers.title: Exploratory radiomics analysis of T1-weighted and FLAIR MRI in relation to Parkinson's disease motor subtypes.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease motor subtypes, tremor-dominant (TD) and postural instability/gait difficulty (PIGD), differ in disease trajectory and prognosis, yet their classification depends on MDS-UPDRS-based clinical ratings that are susceptible to inter-rater variability and medication state.
papers.summary: This study applies exploratory radiomics analysis to T1-weighted and FLAIR MRI scans to investigate whether imaging features can distinguish between Parkinson's disease motor subtypes (tremor-dominant vs. postural instability/gait difficulty). The work aims to address limitations of current clinical rating-based subtyping, which is subject to inter-rater variability and medication effects. As an exploratory analysis, it assesses the potential of radiomic features as objective imaging biomarkers for motor subtype classification.

papers.title: Efficacy and exploratory treatment-response modeling of acupuncture for acute migraine based on DIA proteomics: a study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: According to estimates from the 2019 Global Burden of Disease (GBD) study, approximately 1.1 billion people worldwide suffer from migraine, with a prevalence rate of about 14% to 15%. Despite the development of various medications for different types of migraine, such as acetaminophen and caffeine combination preparations, most patients still experience suboptimal symptom control. Therefore, identifying effective and safer alternative treatments holds significant clinical importance. Acupuncture was formally recommended by the World Health Organization as a migraine therapy as early as 1979. I
papers.summary: This paper presents a study protocol for a randomized controlled trial testing acupuncture as a treatment for acute migraine, using data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics to explore treatment-response biomarkers. The goal is to assess acupuncture's efficacy and identify protein signatures that may predict or explain individual responses to treatment.

papers.title: RCSB PDB AI Help Desk: retrieval-augmented generation for protein structure deposition support.
papers.abstract: Structural biologists have contributed more than 260 000 experimentally determined three-dimensional structures of biological macromolecules to the Protein Data Bank. Incoming depositions are validated and biocurated by approximately 20 expert biocurators at the collaborating data centers worldwide. Biocurators at the Research Collaboratory for Structural Bioinformatics Protein Data Bank, who process more than 40% of global depositions, face growing difficulty sustaining efficient Help Desk operations, having received roughly 19 000 depositor messages across some 8000 entries in 2025.
papers.summary: The RCSB PDB has developed an AI Help Desk that uses retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to assist structural biologists depositing new structures into the Protein Data Bank. The system aims to ease the burden on expert biocurators, who handled roughly 19,000 depositor messages across 8,000 entries in 2025. It provides automated, context-aware support for deposition questions.

papers.title: An evidence-weighted knowledge framework with path-aware reasoning for personalized lifestyle management in chronic disease.
papers.abstract: Healthy lifestyle management is essential for chronic disease prevention and long-term care. However, evidence linking lifestyle behaviors, biological mechanisms, and health outcomes is dispersed across diverse biomedical sources. This fragmentation makes it difficult for health professionals to efficiently retrieve and interpret evidence needed to inform personalized lifestyle guidance.
papers.summary: The paper proposes an evidence-weighted knowledge framework that integrates fragmented biomedical evidence linking lifestyle behaviors, biological mechanisms, and health outcomes, using path-aware reasoning to support personalized lifestyle management in chronic disease. It aims to help health professionals more efficiently retrieve and interpret evidence for tailored lifestyle guidance.

papers.title: GP-DHT: A dual-head transformer with supervised contrastive learning for shared-gene pretraining and single-cell GRN prediction.
papers.abstract: Gene Regulatory Networks (GRNs) are crucial for understanding cell fate decisions and disease mechanisms. However, inferring GRNs from single-cell RNA sequencing remains challenging due to noise, data sparsity, and species-specific distribution variations. We propose GP-DHT (Gene Pair-Dual Head Transformer), a single-cell GRN inference framework that pre-trains gene representations on a unified shared gene space using the BEELINE datasets of humans and mice. It models gene-cell expression relationships through a multi-relational heterograph and predicts transcription factor (TF)-target regulat
papers.summary: GP-DHT is a dual-head transformer framework that uses supervised contrastive learning to pretrain gene representations on a unified human-mouse shared gene space, then predicts transcription factor-target regulatory relationships from single-cell RNA-seq data. It models gene-cell expression via a multi-relational heterograph to address noise, sparsity, and cross-species distribution shifts in GRN inference.

papers.title: Radiomics and deep learning for immune checkpoint inhibitor outcomes: imaging-derived immune phenotyping and clinical translation across solid tumors.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment of multiple solid tumors, but durable benefit remains restricted to a subset of patients and conventional size-based imaging does not fully capture immune-related response patterns. Radiomics and deep learning offer a route to convert routine CT, MRI, and PET/CT into quantitative biomarkers of tumor phenotype, whole-body heterogeneity, and temporal treatment response. This narrative review critically synthesizes the evidence across solid tumors with an emphasis on four questions that are often separated in the literature: what
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on using radiomics and deep learning to predict immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) outcomes across solid tumors. It argues that routine CT, MRI, and PET/CT imaging can be converted into quantitative biomarkers of tumor phenotype, whole-body heterogeneity, and treatment response, potentially enabling imaging-derived immune phenotyping. The review emphasizes clinical translation challenges and organizes the field around four commonly separated research questions.

papers.title: Explainable growth stage classification of cacao (Theobroma cacao L.) leaves and key feature visualization using vision transformer and transfer learning.
papers.abstract: Accurate and objective plant phenotyping is crucial for optimizing agricultural practices, understanding plant development, and enabling rapid responses to environmental changes. Traditional methods, often relying on visual observation, can be subjective, time-consuming, and may overlook subtle but important differences. This study demonstrates the power of combining digital imaging with deep learning to classify plant material with high accuracy, even when visual differences are minimal. We focused on differentiating between stage D (light green) and stage E (dark green) leaves of cacao (Theo
papers.summary: This study applies a vision transformer with transfer learning to classify cacao leaves into two developmental stages (D and E) that differ only subtly in color, achieving high accuracy where human visual assessment is subjective. The authors also visualize key features driving the model's decisions, making the classification interpretable. The work demonstrates how digital imaging plus deep learning can support objective, automated plant phenotyping.

papers.title: Exploring the key genes of colorectal "adenoma-cancer" based on graph transformer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most lethal malignancies worldwide, and the precise identification of biomarkers from colonic adenoma to cancer is of great significance for preventing the development of adenocarcinoma. Given that existing methods inadequately capture the topological network relationships among genes, this study proposes a graph neural network model based on multifeature learning, named ChebTs, to investigate the correlation between key genes involved in the colorectal "adenoma-cancer" transition. The GSE41657 and GSE31905 datasets from the GEO database were stratified in
papers.summary: This study introduces ChebTs, a graph transformer-based neural network that integrates multiple gene features to identify key genes driving the transition from colorectal adenoma to cancer. Using GEO datasets GSE41657 and GSE31905, the model aims to better capture topological gene network relationships than prior methods for biomarker discovery. The work is a computational methodology contribution focused on colorectal cancer progression.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Stem Cell Research: From Biological Data to Clinical Translation.
papers.abstract: Stem cell (SC) research plays a central role in disease modeling and regenerative medicine, yet its clinical translation remains challenged by biological heterogeneity, incomplete cellular maturation, stringent quality-control requirements, and increasingly complex biological and clinical data. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a powerful computational approach for extracting biologically meaningful information from these data, enabling quantitative characterization of SC behavior and predictive modeling across diverse experimental and translational applications. This review presents a unif
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning is being applied across stem cell research, from analyzing complex biological data to supporting clinical translation. It highlights how ML can quantitatively characterize stem cell behavior and build predictive models despite challenges like heterogeneity and incomplete maturation. The work provides a unified overview of current methods and translational applications.

papers.title: Bio-Inspired Artificial Intelligence Multimorbidity Score for Human-Machine Clinical Risk Stratification.
papers.abstract: Multimorbidity is strongly associated with mortality, but existing comorbidity indices often generalize poorly across populations because they depend on fixed disease lists and context-specific weights. We developed the large-language-model-based multimorbidity score (LLM-MMS), a prompt-based large-language-model-derived multimorbidity phenotype score, as a bio-inspired artificial intelligence score for human-machine clinical risk stratification and evaluated it for all-cause mortality prediction in 770,439 adults from 9 international longitudinal cohorts. Harmonized participant-level data wer
papers.summary: The authors developed LLM-MMS, a prompt-based large-language-model-derived multimorbidity score, as a bio-inspired AI tool for clinical risk stratification. They evaluated it for all-cause mortality prediction in 770,439 adults across 9 international longitudinal cohorts, aiming to overcome the poor generalizability of fixed disease-list comorbidity indices.
